purpose: Show the exact reported effects of the leading colic interventions on daily crying and fussing time versus placebo, including the contradictory results for Lactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938.
title: What moves the needle on colic crying
story: The individual-participant meta-analysis of four double-blind trials reported 25.4 minutes per day less crying and fussing with L. reuteri DSM 17938, driven by breastfed infants.
The largest single trial, which uniquely included formula-fed infants, reported 49 minutes per day more crying and fussing in the probiotic group.
Pooled lactase-drop trials reported no significant effect.
All three estimates carry wide 95% confidence intervals; populations and feeding modes differ, so the rows must be read as separate experiments, not one pooled effect.

rows.label: L. reuteri, 4 pooled trials
rows.detail: n=345, effect driven by breastfed infants

observed: All plotted values are the reported adjusted mean differences and 95% confidence intervals from the cited publications.
The Sung 2014 estimate is the trial's reported 49 minutes per day more crying or fussing in the probiotic group at one month.
inferred: The contrast between the pooled estimate and the largest trial reflects the breastfed versus formula-fed difference reported in the individual-participant meta-analysis.
layout_notes: Single open panel on a white landscape canvas: three horizontal dot-and-whisker rows over one shared linear minutes-per-day axis.
A dashed vertical reference line at zero labelled '0 = no difference'; directional cues 'less crying' left and 'more crying' right under the axis.
Row labels and study details in black Arial at the left; each exact estimate printed beside its dot.
Compact key at the bottom expanding the dot, whisker, and CI encodings.
constraints: Arial throughout; smallest text at least 26 px at a 1536 px canvas width.

Do not pool the rows visually or imply one combined effect.
